- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Soreness and cracked skin on hands, possibly related to cleaning products and not wearing gloves at work as a housekeeper. Recent job change noted.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Symptoms began 3-4 months ago; have worsened to the point of impacting job duties.
- ENT symptoms: Not applicable.

**Assessment:**
- Clinical impression: Suspected contact dermatitis related to occupational exposure to cleaning products without glove protection. Contributing factors include extended exposure and minimal personal protective equipment use.

**Plan:**
- Immediate actions taken/advised: Advised to consistently wear gloves while cleaning. Prescription of steroid creams and stronger emollients to be applied 3-4 times daily.
- Specific instructions provided to patient/caregiver: Follow up if symptoms do not improve in 10-14 days or if they worsen. Prescription sent to pharmacy.
- Escalation criteria/red flags: Return for earlier evaluation if symptoms worsen or spread.
- Follow-up: Re-evaluation in 1-2 weeks if no improvement.
